subject: Embeddings Mirror + Fallback: EU failover pattern proposal
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex@pinecone.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@pinecone.io
Date: 2026-10-10T08:12:00Z
Subject: Service pattern question: EU eviction/backpressure + Redwood fallback

Hi Irene,

Quick note from the Pinecone reliability team — over the last 48hrs we saw a transient eviction wave in our eu-west cluster tied to a noisy indexing job. A few mutual customers asked how Redwood would behave if their primary Pinecone index returned partial results or raised throttling at the vector store layer.

Specifically they want to understand:
- How Redwood routes queries when the partner index becomes degraded
- Whether you support transparent read-failover to an alternate store (pgvector / S3) and the latency/consistency tradeoffs
- What operational configuration (TTL, fallback priorities, cache prefixes) we should recommend in our joint docs

Can we get a short proposal from your partner/ops side so we can include it in a runbook we share with customers? We're aiming to publish guidance by end of next week.

Thanks — happy to sync if it's easier.

Best,
Alex Reynolds
Partner Reliability, Pinecone

--
Attachment: incident-summary-20261008.txt (text)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex@pinecone.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Service pattern question: EU eviction/backpressure + Redwood fallback

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and the incident note. We definitely want aligned guidance here; customers get nervous when the vector tier is noisy.

High-level proposal below; attaching a short draft PDF that spells this out for joint runbooks (eu-mirror-fallback-draft.pdf). Ben/Vanessa/Connor — please review technical/ops notes and the attached patch I asked Ben to prepare.

Summary proposal (short):
1) Active read preference: primary external vector store (Pinecone)
2) Synchronous mirror for critical index writes: duplicate embeddings to a lightweight pgvector per-region as a warm replica (writes are acknowledged after both writes succeed for critical workflows)
3) Cold fallback: if primary read fails or latency > configured SLO, Redwood runtime transparently routes reads to regional pgvector; if pgvector cannot satisfy, fallback to S3 cold store (eventual) with an explicit degrade flag in the response header so apps can signal degraded UX
4) Cache & prefixing: Redis prefix cache for hot queries with TTL tuned by qps; prefix caching prevents repeated cold reads during recovery windows
5) Rollback and evictions: when Pinecone signals eviction/backpressure, Redwood will: switch read priority, surface event in Console, and trigger a canary-only reindex to warm pgvector if failover persists >10m

Operational knobs we recommend documenting:
- latency_threshold_ms (default 300ms)
- fallthrough_order: [pinecone, pgvector, s3] (configurable per-account)
- pgvector_sync_mode: async|sync (default async, recommend sync for regulated customers)
- mirror_ttl_seconds for the Redis prefix cache

Next steps:
- Ben: add config diff and routing policy (attached routing-policy.patch)
- Vanessa: ensure Console events and incident UI map to the Pinecone status page (cc: ops links)
- Connor: draft the customer-facing paragraph and SLO impact note (slo-impact-notes.txt attached)

Alex: if that aligns we'll schedule a quick 30m to lock the wording and publish joint guidance.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Storage Partnerships, Redwood Inference

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Service pattern question: EU eviction/backpressure + Redwood fallback

Irene / team — attaching the routing-policy.patch and a short implementation note. High-level tech notes below.

Quoted for context:
> Alex Reynolds: "Specifically they want to understand how Redwood routes queries when the partner index becomes degraded"

Implementation notes (technical):
- Routing logic: runtime evaluates response latency + error rate from helper that polls partner health. Pseudocode:
  if (pinecone.latency > latency_threshold_ms || pinecone.error_rate > error_rate_threshold) {
    prefer(pgvector);
  }
- Dual-write: use a buffered write stream to ensure writes to Pinecone and pgvector are attempted in parallel. Fallback to enqueue-for-retry on pgvector failures. For synchronous mode we wait for both write ACKs with a 1500ms bounded timeout.
- Consistency: tag embeddings with source_version and vector_store_hint header so queries can detect mixed-state responses. Responses include "X-Redwood-Degraded: true" when serving from cold/s3 fallback.
- Reindex canary: when failover exceeds 10 minutes we trigger a low-qps canary reindex from pinecone snapshot -> pgvector with throttled workers (configurable).
- Observability: emit metric redwood.vector.fallback.count, vector.fallback.latency.ms, and a per-account last-fallback-timestamp that shows up in Console.

Ops caveats:
- S3 fallback is eventually consistent and can be 5-60s slower depending on object lifecycle. Recommend using S3 only for archival or very tolerant UX patterns.
- pgvector sizing: for hot replicas target 2-3x peak qps headroom in region to avoid immediate thrashing during failover.

I've included a minimal patch for the routing policy and a short config example in routing-policy.patch. Vanessa/Connor — please flag anything you want adjusted before we send to Alex.

Ben Carter
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
